chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Ja'far al-Himyari, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada bin Sadaqa, from Ja'far bin Muhammad, from his father, from his fathers, peace be upon them,

that he said: The Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: I entered Paradise, and then I saw that most of its people were stupid. He said: I said: What is the stupid? So he said: The rational in good things, the unaware in evil things, who fasts, in every month, three days.

key_terms.الْبَلَهَ: Simplicity or naivety, interpreted here as wisdom in good and heedlessness of evil

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'al-balah' in the hadith about Paradise?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to clarify the paradoxical term 'al-balah' (often translated as simpletons), redefining it not as intellectual deficiency but as spiritual simplicity and consistency in worship. This interpretation highlights the Shia emphasis on the virtue of *ghafla* (heedlessness) regarding worldly distractions and minor sins, while maintaining rigorous devotion, such as the monthly fasting of the white days (Ayyam al-Beed).
